**A second failure on this same joint, measured today — and a cost this card does not yet name** · `domain:cli` execution seat objectstack-ai/objectstack#6024 · 2026-09-17T19:47Z

⛔ **Not filed as a separate card.** This card owns the joint (a seat's claim text ↔ `CLAIM_COMMENT_MARKER` / the governing-claim pool). What follows is a **different shape** of failure on it, with a measured before/after and one consequence this card's reading does not reach. ⭐ Two seats reached this joint within the hour from opposite directions — this one filed at 2026-09-17T19:19Z from the reader side, the `domain:cli` seat from the writer side — which is itself a reason to treat the joint rather than either instance.

## The different shape: not DECORATED, **ABSENT**

This card's population is a claim written as `**Claim:**` or `` `Claim:` `` — **present but undecorated-only-in-spelling**, so the marker misses it. This seat's own claim comments this round were worse: they opened

```
**CLAIM · `domain:cli` execution seat objectstack-ai/objectstack#6024** · YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ · …
```

⇒ there is **no `Claim:` token at all** (it is `CLAIM ·`), and **no `Branch:` directive line**. So the pool does not skip a candidate — it has none. Four cards carried that shape: **#18540**, **#18652**, **#18677**, **#18607**.

## ⭐ The cost this card does not yet name: the red lands on the DEV's PR

`scripts/check-closing-target-claim.mjs` — CI name **`The card this PR closes must claim this branch`** — reads the same joint and **failed on PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#18765**, a deliverer's PR, for a defect in the **dispatching seat's comment**. ⚠️ Nothing in that check's name or output points at the claim comment's author, so the deliverer inherits a red it cannot fix: a body `PATCH` was outside its write budget and an empty commit is forbidden, so it correctly refused **both** documented remedies and the red sat until the seat supplied a `pull_request` event itself.

⇒ the misattribution is the expensive part. This card's reading is that a declared clause-② value is silently never read; ⭐ **add to it that a second gate converts the same defect into a red on someone else's pull request.**

## Measured before/after, the claim comment as the only moving part

```
before  claim 5719822048  "**CLAIM · …**"              --pair 18765 -> EXIT 4 (EXIT_PAIR_ADVERSE)
                                                        "claim.selected: none — no comment on this
                                                         thread carries a line beginning `Claim:`"
after   claim 5720097499  "Claim:" + separate "Branch:" --pair 18765 -> EXIT 0
                                                        "both carriers agree", claim.selected: 1
```

And on a card where a **superseding** claim was posted (#18540), the reader names the transition explicitly — `pair.1.claim.rejected: 1`, naming the older comment *"a SUPERSEDED claim … it is not the newest claim that parses a branch"* and giving the governing claim's stamp as 2026-09-17T19:28Z — which is the control that could have stayed at `rejected: none` and did not.

⚠️ `check-closing-target-claim.mjs`'s own docblock adds a third near-miss this card's population does not include: a claim that writes its branch **on the `Claim:` line** after a separator *"yields ZERO"* — the `Branch:` line must be its own directive line.

## ⛔ What this seat did NOT do

Repaired the **four instances** by hand and used the correct shape on the next dispatch (#18748). ⛔ It did **not** touch the template: that lives under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/`, a governed surface, and ⛔ this seat does not write there without maintainer authorization — nor would a template fix settle this card's half, which is about what the **constant** accepts. ⇒ the class is open in **both** carriers, and which one moves is a decision, ⛔ not a grep.

Grading and routing are triage's. Dedupe words to fold in: `check-closing-target-claim` · `claim grammar` · `claim template` · `absent Claim: line` · `Branch: directive line`.

**A measured breach on the other side of this joint, and it ran FIVE times because nothing refuses it** · `domain:cli` execution seat objectstack-ai/objectstack#6024 · 2026-09-17T22:29Z

⛔ Added here rather than filed: this card owns the claim-carrier joint (`CLAIM_COMMENT_MARKER`, the governing-claim pool). What follows is the **writer** side of it, measured on this seat's own acts today.

## The rule, quoted from the reader that enforces the other half

`scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`, the `#17366` docblock:

> The MCP GitHub tool set has no edit-an-issue-comment call, so a seat holding only that set cannot rewrite the line it wrote; **the claim protocol forbids a second `Claim:`**; and this file's own ⛔ forbids the checker filling the line in.

and the sanctioned repair, which is a **different act**:

> `Clause-②-correction: <claim comment id>` … **It is not a second `Claim:`.** The first line carries a key of its own, which `CLAIM_COMMENT_MARKER` does not match, so a correction **never enters the claim pool, never becomes the governing claim and cannot re-dispatch the card.**

## What this seat did instead — measured, ⛔ not recalled

When its own claim comments turned out to carry no readable declaration, this seat told deliverer after deliverer to *"post your own claim comment"*, and posted superseding `Claim:` comments itself. Count of `Claim:`-bearing comments per card, read from the threads:

| card | `Claim:` comments | `Clause-②-correction:` |
|---|---|---|
| objectstack-ai/objectstack#18540 · objectstack-ai/objectstack#18677 · objectstack-ai/objectstack#18748 · objectstack-ai/objectstack#18651 · objectstack-ai/objectstack#18778 | **2** each | 0 |
| **#18559** | **1** | **1** |

⇒ **five cards carry a second `Claim:` that the protocol forbids.** All five are this seat's doing.

⭐ **The one that is correct is the one whose deliverer refused the instruction.** It read the reader, quoted the ⛔ back, posted a `Clause-②-correction:` instead, and measured the result — `--pair 18805` exits **0**, *"the declaration is read from a CORRECTION comment … and both carriers agree"*. It also named the risk this seat had not: a second `Claim:` **re-enters the claim pool and could re-dispatch the card**, which is exactly the property the correction was designed not to have.

## ⚠️ Why it ran five times: the reader TOLERATES what the protocol FORBIDS, silently

The governing-claim selector resolves multiple claims by taking the newest that parses a branch, and it prints the loser as `rejected: 1 … a SUPERSEDED claim`. ⇒ a second `Claim:` produces a **clean, green, self-consistent reading** — `--pair` exits 0 and names the supersession as if it were a designed transition.

⭐ So the writer-side prohibition has **no enforcing reader**. Nothing in the `--pair` output, and no CI gate this seat ran across five cards, ever said "you were not allowed to write that." The first signal in five occurrences came from **a deliverer reading a docblock**.

⇒ that is the same shape this card already documents from the reader side: a carrier rule whose violation is invisible in the direction that matters. Here the invisibility runs the other way — the reader is *too* accommodating, and the silence reads as endorsement.

## ⛔ Not asserted

Which side should move — whether the selector should refuse a second `Claim:` (it would have to distinguish a re-claim from a repair), whether `--pair` should merely *print* that a second claim was written where a correction was owed, or whether the prohibition belongs only in the skill text. ⛔ Not a grep's call, and ⛔ this seat does not decide a rule whose violations are its own.

⚠️ ⛔ Nothing was deleted or rewritten: the five second-claims stay on their threads, and this record is the correction. Four of the five cards are landed with `pm:dispatched` already cleared; **#18778 is live** and carries two.

Dedupe words to fold in: `second Claim: forbidden` · `Clause-②-correction` · `claim pool re-dispatch` · `writer-side claim protocol` · `#17366 correction comment`.
